title: Message Deduplication
description: Learn deduplication strategies to detect and discard duplicate messages in distributed queue systems.

data.text: Deduplication is the practice of identifying when the same message has been received more than once and safely ignoring subsequent copies. It sits at the intersection of idempotency and message ordering: without deduplication, an idempotent consumer is a safeguard, but deduplication at the broker or consumer level can reduce waste and simplify downstream logic.

data.title: Deduplication layers
items: Broker-level: the broker discards duplicates before delivery
Consumer-level: the consumer checks each message before processing
Application-level: business logic absorbs duplicates gracefully

data.text: Amazon SQS FIFO queues support content-based deduplication natively. When enabled, SQS computes a SHA-256 hash of the message body and stores it for five minutes. If another message with the same body arrives within that window, SQS silently drops it. For custom deduplication, supply a MessageDeduplicationId yourself.

data.title: C# — SQS FIFO with content-based deduplication
data.content: Enable content-based deduplication on the queue and send messages without manually computing IDs.

data.text: When the broker does not support deduplication, the consumer must handle it. A common pattern is to maintain a set of recently seen message IDs in Redis or the database. The Bloom filter is a memory-efficient alternative when you can tolerate a small false-positive rate.

data.title: Node.js — Bloom filter for message deduplication
data.content: Use the 'bloom-filters' package to check for duplicates with minimal memory.

data.title: Deduplication Window Limits
data.text: SQS FIFO deduplication only covers a five-minute window. Outside that window, identical messages are treated as distinct. Design your producers to keep deduplication IDs stable and collisions low.

items.question: Can I rely on content-based deduplication alone?
items.answer: Only if messages are truly identical. If timestamps or trace IDs differ, content-based deduplication will not catch them. Use explicit MessageDeduplicationId when possible.

items.question: Should I deduplicate at the broker or consumer?
items.answer: Broker-level deduplication reduces network traffic and consumer load. Consumer-level is more flexible and works with any broker. Many production systems use both.

items.question: What happens if the Bloom filter has a false positive?
items.answer: A legitimate message is discarded. Mitigate this by following the Bloom check with a Redis set lookup, which is exact.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SQS FIFO supports native content-based deduplication with a 5-minute window
Redis sets provide exact deduplication with TTL-based expiry
Bloom filters reduce memory usage at the cost of false positives
Combine layers: broker dedup + consumer dedup + idempotent writes
data.takeaway: Deduplication is cheaper than processing duplicates. Choose the right data structure for your scale and accuracy requirements.
